# Staying Productive When Your Couch Is Right There

Working from home should be the dream, right? No commute, no pants required. But somehow you blink and it's 3 PM and you've accomplished exactly one task and watched half a season of whatever's trending.

Been there.

Here's what actually helps me get stuff done:

**Create a fake commute.** I know it sounds silly, but walk around the block before you start work. It tricks your brain into "work mode" instead of "I'm still in pajamas at noon" mode.

**Get dressed.** Doesn't have to be fancy. Just not the same clothes you slept in. There's something about changing that signals to your brain that the day has actually started.

**Set ridiculous boundaries.** My kitchen is off-limits during work hours except for scheduled breaks. Otherwise I'll migrate there seventeen times before lunch and suddenly I've reorganized the entire pantry instead of finishing that report.

**Use the Pomodoro thing.** Twenty-five minutes of focused work, then a five-minute break. Sounds simple because it is. And it works.

**Have an ending ritual.** Shut your laptop. Close the door to your workspace if you have one. Do *something* that marks the day as done. Otherwise work just bleeds into evening and you're answering emails at 9 PM while pretending to watch a movie.

**Accept that some days are weird.** You're going to have off days. That's fine. Working from home isn't about being productive 100% of the time—it's about finding a rhythm that doesn't make you want to throw your laptop out the window.

The goal isn't perfection. It's just getting through the day without your couch winning.
